Supports: Where the product provides closed functionality that is operable through a keyboard or keyboard interface, the component with the input focus is visually indicated, so that users can see which element will respond to input.
Partially Supports: Where the product provides closed functionality that is operable through a keyboard or keyboard interface, in most cases the component with the input focus is visually indicated.
Does not Support: Where the product provides closed functionality that is operable through a keyboard or keyboard interface, in most, if not all, cases the component with the input focus is not visually indicated.
Not Applicable: The product does not provide closed functionality; keyboard focus is handled through the platform and assistive technologies, so this requirement does not apply.

Supports: Where the product provides closed functionality that is operated through speech input, at least one mode of operation is provided that does not require the user to produce speech.
Partially Supports: Where the product provides closed functionality that is operated through speech input, in most cases at least one mode of operation is provided that does not require the user to produce speech.
Does not Support: Where the product provides closed functionality that is operated through speech input, in most, if not all, cases no mode of operation is provided that does not require the user to produce speech.
Not Applicable: The product does not require speech input to operate; all functionality can be operated through standard input methods, so this requirement does not apply.

Supports: Where the product provides documented accessibility features, it provides a means to activate those features that can itself be operated by the users who need them, without requiring the very ability the feature is intended to support.
Partially Supports: Where the product provides documented accessibility features, most of those features can be activated by a means that can itself be operated by the users who need them.
Does not Support: Where the product provides documented accessibility features, most, if not all, of those features cannot be activated by a means that can itself be operated by the users who need them.
Not Applicable: The product does not have any documented accessibility features that require activation. Accessibility support is provided through the platform and assistive technologies, which do not need to be activated within the product.

Supports: Where the product uses biological characteristics for user identification or control, it does not rely on a single biological characteristic, and it provides at least one mode of operation that does not require biometrics.
Partially Supports: Where the product uses biological characteristics for user identification or control, in most cases it does not rely on a single biological characteristic and provides an alternative mode of operation that does not require biometrics.
Does not Support: Where the product uses biological characteristics for user identification or control, in most, if not all, cases it relies on a single biological characteristic and does not provide an alternative mode of operation that does not require biometrics.
Not Applicable: The product does not use biometric forms of user identification or control. All functionality is accessible through standard input methods (keyboard, mouse, UI).

Checkpoint: 5.4 Preservation of accessibility information during conversion
Supports: Where the product converts information or communication from one format to another, the accessibility information present in the source is preserved in the output to the extent that equivalent mechanisms exist in the destination format.
Partially Supports: Where the product converts information or communication from one format to another, in most cases the accessibility information present in the source is preserved in the output where equivalent mechanisms exist in the destination format.
Does not Support: Where the product converts information or communication from one format to another, in most, if not all, cases the accessibility information present in the source is not preserved in the output even where equivalent mechanisms exist in the destination format.
Not Applicable: The product does not convert information or communication from one format to another. As no conversion of accessibility information takes place, there is no accessibility information to be preserved.

Supports: Where the product has operable parts that require grasping, pinching, or twisting of the wrist to operate, an alternative accessible means of operation that does not require these actions is provided.
Partially Supports: Where the product has operable parts, in most cases an alternative means of operation that does not require grasping, pinching, or twisting of the wrist is provided.
Does not Support: Where the product has operable parts, in most, if not all, cases no alternative means of operation is provided that does not require grasping, pinching, or twisting of the wrist.
Not Applicable: The product does not have physical operable parts; all functionality is operated through standard input methods, so this requirement does not apply.

Supports: Where the product has physical operable parts, those parts are discernible without vision through tactile or auditory means.
Partially Supports: Where the product has physical operable parts, in most cases those parts are discernible without vision through tactile or auditory means.
Does not Support: Where the product has physical operable parts, in most, if not all, cases those parts are not discernible without vision through tactile or auditory means.
Not Applicable: The product does not have physical operable parts; all functionality is operated through standard input methods, so this requirement does not apply.

Supports: Where the product has a locking or toggle control that is presented visually, the status of that control can be determined through touch or sound without requiring vision.
Partially Supports: Where the product has locking or toggle controls, in most cases the status of the control can be determined through touch or sound without requiring vision.
Does not Support: Where the product has locking or toggle controls, in most, if not all, cases the status of the control cannot be determined through touch or sound without requiring vision.
Not Applicable: The product does not have physical locking or toggle controls; control status is conveyed through the platform and assistive technologies, so this requirement does not apply.

Supports: Where the product has a locking or toggle control, the status of that control is visually discernible, so that it can be determined visually.
Partially Supports: Where the product has locking or toggle controls, in most cases the status of the control is visually discernible.
Does not Support: Where the product has locking or toggle controls, in most, if not all, cases the status of the control is not visually discernible.
Not Applicable: The product does not have physical locking or toggle controls; control status is conveyed through the platform and assistive technologies, so this requirement does not apply.

Supports: Where the product provides a key repeat function, the user is able to turn off key repeat or adjust the key repeat delay to at least two seconds.
Partially Supports: Where the product provides a key repeat function, in most cases the user is able to turn off key repeat or adjust the key repeat delay to at least two seconds.
Does not Support: Where the product provides a key repeat function, in most, if not all, cases the user is not able to turn off key repeat or adjust the key repeat delay.
Not Applicable: The product does not provide a physical keyboard with a key repeat function; text entry is handled through the platform and assistive technologies, so this requirement does not apply.

Supports: Where the product has a keyboard or keypad, the user is able to adjust the time period during which two presses of the same key are not accepted as two separate key presses.
Partially Supports: Where the product has a keyboard or keypad, in most cases the user is able to adjust the time period during which two presses of the same key are not accepted as two separate key presses.
Does not Support: Where the product has a keyboard or keypad, in most, if not all, cases the user is not able to adjust the time period during which two presses of the same key are accepted as two separate key presses.
Not Applicable: The product does not have a physical keyboard or keypad; text entry is handled through the platform and assistive technologies, so this requirement does not apply.

Supports: Where the product's operation requires simultaneous user actions, an alternative mode of operation is provided that does not require more than one action at a time.
Partially Supports: Where the product's operation requires simultaneous user actions, in most cases an alternative mode of operation is provided that does not require more than one action at a time.
Does not Support: Where the product's operation requires simultaneous user actions, in most, if not all, cases no alternative mode of operation is provided that can be performed with a single action.
Not Applicable: The product does not require simultaneous user actions to operate; all functionality can be operated through single actions, so this requirement does not apply.

Supports: Where the product provides features for accessibility, it maintains the privacy of people who use these features at the same level as other users.
Partially Supports: Where the product provides features for accessibility, it maintains the privacy of most people who use these features at the same level as other users.
Does not Support: The product provides features for accessibility; however, the privacy of most, if not all, people who use these features is not maintained at the same level as other users.
Not Applicable: The product does not provide any specific accessibility features that impact the user's privacy.

Supports: The product provides closed functionality for auditory output (including speech). However, it allows such output to be provided through only integral auditory features such as speakers or by a personal headset that can be connected through a 3.5 mm audio jack, or another industry standard connection, without requiring the use of vision, so people or who are blind or have low vision and others who use a screen reader, can access audible output.
Partially Supports: The product provides closed functionality for auditory output (including speech), and it allows most auditory output to be provided through only integral auditory features such as speakers or by a personal headset that can be connected through a 3.5 mm audio jack, or another industry standard connection, without requiring the use of vision.
Does not Support: The product provides closed functionality for auditory output (including speech), and it does not allow most, if not all, auditory output to be provided through only integral auditory features such as speakers or by a personal headset that can be connected through a 3.5 mm audio jack, or another industry standard connection, without requiring the use of vision.
Not Applicable: The product allows auditory output (including speech) to be conveyed by outside mechanisms (including speakers, handsets, and earbuds).

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: The ICT renders text available to assistive technologies including information about the text attributes and the boundary (where the text starts and ends).
Partially Supports: The ICT renders most text available to assistive technologies, including information about the text attributes and the boundary (where the text starts and ends).
Does not Support: The ICT does not render most, if not all, text available to assistive technologies, including information about the text attributes and the boundary (where the text starts and ends).
Not Applicable: The ICT does not have a user interface or render text to the screen.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: The ICT has a user interface that provides a list of actions that can be executed by the user. This list of actions is programmatically determinable by assistive technologies.
Partially Supports: The ICT has a user interface that provides a list of actions that can be executed by the user, and most of those actions are programmatically determinable by assistive technologies.
Does not Support: The ICT has a user interface that provides a list of actions that can be executed by the user, but most, if not all, of those actions are not programmatically determinable by assistive technologies.
Not Applicable: The ICT does not have a user interface or a list of actions that can be executed by the user.

Supports: When the website or application displays captions for a video that has synchronized audio, the captions are synchronized with the audio, so people who are deaf and others who need captions are able to access the information conveyed in the audio track.
Partially Supports: When the website or application displays captions for most videos that have synchronized audio, the captions are synchronized with the audio.
Does not Support: When the website or application displays captions for a video that has synchronized audio, the captions are not synchronized with the audio.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not contain video that has synchronized audio.

Supports: When the website or application displays captions for a video that has synchronized audio, the display characteristics (such as color, font, or size) of the caption text can be modified by the user so people with low vision or color blindness can adapt the caption text to meet their needs.
Partially Supports: When the website or application displays captions for video that has synchronized audio, the display characteristics (such as color, font, or size) of most caption text can be modified by the user.
Does not Support: When the website or application displays captions for video that has synchronized audio, the display characteristics (such as color, font, or size) of caption text cannot be modified by the user.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not contain video that has synchronized audio.

Supports: When the website or application displays captions for a video that has synchronized audio, the captions can be announced as spoken output.
Partially Supports: When the website or application displays captions for a video that has synchronized audio, most captions can be announced as spoken output.
Does not Support: When the website or application displays captions for a video that has synchronized audio, most, if not all, captions cannot be announced as spoken output.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not contain video that has synchronized audio.

Supports: When the website or application displays video that has synchronized audio, a mechanism is provided to select and play audio description, so people who are blind or have low vision and others who cannot view the video can hear a description of the action and other visual information not conveyed in the soundtrack.
Partially Supports: The website or application allows the user to play audio description if it is available for most videos that have synchronized audio.
Does not Support: The website or application does not allow the user to play audio description if it is available for a video that has synchronized audio.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not contain video that has synchronized audio.

Supports: When the website or application plays audio description for video that has synchronized audio, the audio description is synchronized with the audio soundtrack and the video, so people who are blind or have low vision and other who cannot view the video can hear a description of the action and other visual information not conveyed in the soundtrack.
Partially Supports: When the website or application plays audio description for most videos that have synchronized audio, the audio description is synchronized with the audio soundtrack and the video.
Does not Support: When the website or application plays audio description for a video that has synchronized audio, the audio description is not synchronized with the audio soundtrack and the video.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not contain video that has synchronized audio.

Supports: When the website or application transmits, converts, or records video with synchronized audio, data associated with audio description is preserved, so people who are blind or have low vision and other who cannot view the video are able to hear a description of the action and other visual information not conveyed in the soundtrack.
Partially Supports: In most cases, when the website or application transmits, converts, or records video with synchronized audio, data associated with audio description is preserved.
Does not Support: In most, if not all, cases, when the website or application transmits, converts, or records video with synchronized audio, data associated with audio descriptions is not preserved
Not Applicable: The website or application does not transmit, convert, or record video that has synchronized audio.

Checkpoint: 7.3 User controls for captions and audio description
Supports: Each multimedia player provides the caption and audio description controls at the same level as other media controls, so people who are deaf and others who need closed captions are able to find the controls and activate the captions and people who are blind or have low vision and others who need audio descriptions are able to find the controls and activate the descriptions.
Partially Supports: In most instances, multimedia players provide closed caption and audio description controls at the same level as other media controls.
Does not Support: In most, if not all, instances, multimedia players do not provide closed caption and audio description controls at the same level as other media controls.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not contain media with an audio component that has closed captions or media with a video component that has audio description.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: The ICT is software that provides a user interface and makes all elements' role, state, boundary, name and description programmatically determinable.
Partially Supports: The ICT is software that provides a user interface and makes most elements' role, state, boundary, name and description programmatically determinable.
Does not Support: The ICT is software that provides a user interface but does not make most, if not all, elements' role, state, boundary, name and description programmatically determinable.
Not Applicable: The ICT is not software that provides a user interface.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: The ICT is assistive technology and provides a set of documented platform services to interoperate with assistive technology.
Partially Supports: The ICT is assistive technology and provides most of the documented platform services needed to interoperate with assistive technology.
Does not Support: The ICT is assistive technology but does not provide most, if not all, of the documented platform services needed to interoperate with assistive technology.
Not Applicable: The ICT is not assistive technology.

Supports: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.
Partially Supports: When most user interface components receive keyboard focus, each component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.
Does not Support: When most, if not all, user interface components receive keyboard focus, each component is entirely hidden due to author-created content.
Not Applicable: This success criterion technically doesn't apply to native mobile applications.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: The ICT allows user control over platform accessibility features.
Partially Supports: The ICT allows user control over most platform accessibility features.
Does not Support: The ICT does not allow user control over most, if not all, platform accessibility features.
Not Applicable: There are no platform features that are defined in the platform documentation as accessibility features intended for users.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: In its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application prompts content creators to make the content accessible during or after creation, so the information necessary to make portions of the content accessible may be added and that content will be available to some people with disabilities.
Partially Supports: In most instances, in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application prompts content creators to make the content accessible during or after creation, so the information necessary to make portions of the content accessible may be added, and that content will be available to some people with disabilities.
Does not Support: In most, if not all, instances in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application does not prompt content creators to make the content accessible during or after creation, so the information necessary to make portions of the content accessible may not be added and that content will not be available to some people with disabilities.
Not Applicable: The website or application is not an authoring tool.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 12 - Documentation and Support Svcs.
Supports: Documentation is provided for the website or application that includes information on its accessibility features or on features that make it compatible with assistive technology, so people with disabilities will know these features exist and how to use them.
Partially Supports: Documentation is provided for the website or application that includes most information on its accessibility features or on features that make it compatible with assistive technology, so people with disabilities will know these features exist and how to use them.
Does not Support: Documentation is provided for the website or application, but it does not include most, if not all, information on its accessibility features or on features that make it compatible with assistive technology, so people with disabilities will not know these features exist, nor how to use them.
Not Applicable: Documentation is not provided for the website or application.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 12 - Documentation and Support Svcs.
Supports: Documentation provided for the website or application is available in digital formats that conform to WCAG 2.1, so the documentation and the information it contains are accessible to people with disabilities.
Partially Supports: Most documentation provided for the website or application is available in at least one digital format that conforms to WCAG 2.1, so the documentation and the information it contains are accessible to people with disabilities.
Does not Support: Documentation provided for the website or application is not available in at least one digital format that conforms to WCAG 2.1, so the documentation and the information it contains may not be accessible to some people with disabilities.
Not Applicable: Documentation is not provided for the website or application.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: The values of user interface elements, whose values can be modified by a user without the use of assistive technology, can be modified by assistive technologies using the input methods of the platform as well as text of user interface elements.
Partially Supports: The values of most user interface elements, whose values can be modified by a user without the use of assistive technology, can be modified by assistive technologies using the input methods of the platform, as well as the text of those user interface elements.
Does not Support: The values of most, if not all, user interface elements, whose values can be modified by a user without the use of assistive technology, cannot be modified by assistive technologies using the input methods of the platform, nor can the text of those user interface elements.
Not Applicable:
The ICT does not have a user interface, 
or The ICT does not have user interface elements that can be modified by the user without the use of assistive technology, or The ICT security requirements do not permit modification of user interface elements.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: The website or application allows users to set or modify color, contrast, font type, and size, and focus the cursor.
Partially Supports: In most instances, the website or application allows users to set or modify color, contrast, font type, and size, and focus the cursor.
Does not Support: In most instances, the website or application does not allow users to set or modify color, contrast, font type, and size, and focus the cursor.
Not Applicable: The ICT does not have a user interface, or The ICT does not have settings for language, color, contrast, font type, font size, or focus cursor, that correspond to platform settings, or The software is designed to be isolated from its underlying platforms

Supports: Prerecorded audio-only (such as MP3 files and audio podcasts) and video-only files have a descriptive text transcript, or the application supports equivalent alternatives to audio and video.
Partially Supports: Most prerecorded audio-only files (such as MP3 files and audio podcasts) and video-only files have a descriptive text transcript.
Does not Support: Most, if not all, prerecorded audio-only files, such as MP3 files, audio podcasts, and video-only files, do not have a descriptive text transcript.
Not Applicable: Prerecorded audio-only and video-only files are not present.

Supports: A method is provided to skip navigation and other page elements that are repeated across web pages.
Partially Supports: On most pages, a method is provided to skip navigation and other page elements that are repeated across web pages.
Does not Support: On most, if not all, pages, a method is not provided to skip navigation and other page elements that are repeated across web pages.
Not Applicable: This success criterion technically doesn't apply to native mobile applications.

Supports: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text and its programmatic context.
Partially Supports: The purpose of most links can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text and its programmatic context.
Does not Support: The purpose of most, if not all, links cannot be determined from the link text alone or from the link text and its programmatic context.
Not Applicable: This success criterion technically doesn't apply to native mobile applications.

Supports: The language of each page is correct and can be determined programmatically.
Partially Supports: On most pages, the language of the page is correct and can be determined programmatically.
Does not Support: On most pages, the language of the page is not correct and/or cannot be determined programmatically.
Not Applicable: This success criterion technically doesn't apply to native mobile applications.

Supports: For WCAG 2.0, 2.1, EN 301 549, and Revised 508 Standards, the September 2023 errata update indicates this criterion is always supported. See the WCAG 2.0 Editorial Errata and the WCAG 2.1 Editorial Errata.
Partially Supports: For WCAG 2.0, 2.1, EN 301 549, and Revised 508 Standards, the September 2023 errata update indicates this criterion is always supported. See the WCAG 2.0 Editorial Errata and the WCAG 2.1 Editorial Errata.
Does not Support: For WCAG 2.0, 2.1, EN 301 549, and Revised 508 Standards, the September 2023 errata update indicates this criterion is always supported. See the WCAG 2.0 Editorial Errata and the WCAG 2.1 Editorial Errata.
Not Applicable: This success criterion technically doesn't apply to native mobile applications.

Supports: If a single-character key shortcut exists, then the single-character key shortcut can be turned off or remapped, or it is only active when the relevant user interface component is in focus.
Partially Supports: In most cases, when a single-character key shortcut exists, then the single-character key shortcut can be turned off or remapped, or it is only active when the relevant user interface component is in focus.
Does not Support: When a single-character key shortcut exists, then the single-character key shortcut cannot be turned off or remapped, and it is active when the relevant user interface component is not in focus.
Not Applicable: This success criterion technically doesn't apply to native mobile applications.

Supports: The purpose for each input field that collects an individual's personal data is programmatically defined based on the WCAG list of Input Purposes for User Interface Components.
Partially Supports: The purpose of most input fields that collect an individual's personal data is programmatically defined based on the WCAG list of Input Purposes for User Interface Components.
Does not Support: The purpose of most, if not all, input fields that collect an individual's personal data is not programmatically defined based on the WCAG list of Input Purposes for User Interface Components.
Not Applicable: This success criterion technically doesn't apply to native mobile applications.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 12 - Documentation and Support Svcs.
Supports: Documentation provided by support services is available in digital formats that conform to WCAG 2.1, so the documentation and the information it contains are accessible to people with disabilities.
Partially Supports: Most documentation provided by support services is available in at least one digital format that conforms to WCAG 2.1, so the documentation and the information it contains are accessible to people with disabilities.
Does not Support: Documentation provided by support services is not available in at least one digital format that conforms to WCAG 2.1, so the documentation and the information it contains may not be accessible to some people with disabilities.
Not Applicable: Documentation is not provided by support services for the website or application.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 12 - Documentation and Support Svcs.
Supports: Support services for the website or application provide accommodations to support people with communication-related disabilities, so people with communication-related disabilities can access needed product support.
Partially Supports: Most support services for the website or application provide accommodations to support people with communication-related disabilities, so people with communication-related disabilities can access needed product support.
Does not Support: Most, if not all, support services for the website or application do not provide accommodations to support people with communication-related disabilities, so at least some people with disabilities cannot access needed product support.
Not Applicable: Support services are not provided for the website or application.

Supports: All functionality is usable with limited manipulation and does not require fine motor control or simultaneous manual operations.
Partially Supports: Most functionality is usable with limited manipulation and does not require fine motor control or simultaneous manual operations.
Does not Support: Most, if not all, functionality is not usable with limited manipulation and/or requires fine motor control or simultaneous manual operations.
Not Applicable: The product does not require manipulation to operate.

Checkpoint: 302.9 With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Supports: The product's functionality is usable by people with limited language, cognitive, and learning abilities. People with cognitive disabilities have varying needs for features that allow them to adapt content and work with assistive technology.
Partially Supports: Most functionality is usable by people with limited language, cognitive, and learning abilities. People with cognitive disabilities have varying needs for features that allow them to adapt content and work with assistive technology.
Does not Support: Most, if not all, functionality is not usable by people with limited language, cognitive, and learning abilities. People with cognitive disabilities have varying needs for features that allow them to adapt content and work with assistive technology.
Not Applicable: The product does not require language, cognitive, or learning ability to operate.

Supports: When objects that allow the user to set their respective properties and/or state are present, the act of setting a property or state is available programmatically, so that it can be perceived and performed using assistive technology.
Partially Supports: For most objects that allow the user to set their respective properties and/or state, the act of setting a property or state is available programmatically, so that it can be perceived and performed using assistive technology.
Does not Support: For most, if not all, objects that allow the user to set their respective properties and/or state, the act of setting a property or state is not available programmatically, so that it cannot be perceived and performed using assistive technology.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not contain objects that allow the user to set their properties and/or state.

Supports: When a page contains an element that acts as a label for another element or has an element that is labeled by another element, each labeling relationship is programmatically determinable, so it can be perceived and conveyed by assistive technology.
Partially Supports: For most elements that act as a label for another element and elements that are labeled by another element, the labeling relationship is programmatically determinable, so it can be perceived and conveyed by assistive technology.
Does not Support: For most, if not all, elements that act as a label for another element and elements that are labeled by another element, the labeling relationship is not programmatically determinable, so it cannot be perceived and conveyed by assistive technology.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not contain an element that acts as a label for another element, and it does not contain an element that is labeled by another element.

Supports: The product offers an alternative user interface that allows users to access all platform (OS and browser) accessibility features.
Partially Supports: The product offers an alternative user interface that allows users to access most platform (OS and browser) accessibility features.
Does not Support: The product offers an alternative user interface that does not allow users to access most, if not all, platform (OS and browser) accessibility features.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not offer an alternative user interface.

Checkpoint: 504.2.1 Preservation of Information Provided for Accessibility in Format Conversion
Supports: In its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application preserves accessibility information when converting content from one format to another, so some or all of the information in the original format necessary to make portions of the content accessible is provided in the new format, and this content will be available to people with disabilities.
Partially Supports: In most instances, in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application preserves accessibility information when converting content from one format to another, so information in the original format necessary to make portions of the content accessible is provided in the new format, and this content will be available to people with disabilities.
Does not Support: In most, if not all, instances in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application does not preserve accessibility information when converting content from one format to another.
Not Applicable: The website or application is not an authoring tool.

Supports: In its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application provides templates that allow the creation of accessible content, so content created using these templates will include content that will be accessible to people with disabilities.
Partially Supports: In most instances, in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application provides templates that allow the creation of accessible content, so content created using these templates will include content that will be accessible to people with disabilities.
Does not Support: In most instances in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application does not provide templates that allow the creation of accessible content, so content created using these templates will include content that will not be accessible to people with disabilities.
Not Applicable: The website or application is not an authoring tool.

Supports: Documentation provided for the website or application is available in digital formats that conform to WCAG 2.0, so the documentation and the information it contains are accessible to people with disabilities.
Partially Supports: Most documentation provided for the website or application is available in at least one digital format that conforms to WCAG 2.0, so the documentation and the information it contains are accessible to people with disabilities.
Does not Support: Documentation provided for the website or application is not available in at least one digital format that conforms to WCAG 2.0, so the documentation and the information it contains may not be accessible to some people with disabilities.
Not Applicable: Documentation is not provided for the website or application.

Checkpoint: 4.2.10 Usage with limited cognition, language or learning
Supports: The product's functionality is usable by people with limited language, cognitive, and learning abilities. People with cognitive disabilities have varying needs for features that allow them to adapt content and work with assistive technology.
Partially Supports: Most functionality is usable by people with limited language, cognitive, and learning abilities. People with cognitive disabilities have varying needs for features that allow them to adapt content and work with assistive technology.
Does not Support: Most, if not all, functionality is not usable by people with limited language, cognitive, and learning abilities. People with cognitive disabilities have varying needs for features that allow them to adapt content and work with assistive technology.
Not Applicable: The product does not require language, cognitive, or learning ability to operate.

Supports: The product provides closed functionality for audio output of visual information and does not permit the use of an outside or add-on screen reader. However, it provides a method to enable that functionality that does not require sight, so people  who are blind or have low vision and others who use a screen reader can enable audio output of visual information.
Partially Supports: The product provides closed functionality for audio output of visual information and does not permit the use of an outside or add-on screen reader, and in most cases, it provides a method to enable that functionality that does not require sight.
Does not Support: The product provides closed functionality for audio output of visual information and does not permit use of an outside or add-on screen reader, and in most, if not all, cases, it does not provide a method to enable that functionality that does not require sight.
Not Applicable: The product allows the use of an outside or add-on screen reader to provide audio output of visual information.

Supports: The website or application allows the user to display captions if they are available for a video that has synchronized audio, so people who are deaf and others who need captions are able to access the information conveyed in the audio track.
Partially Supports: The website or application allows the user to display captions if they are available for most videos that have synchronized audio.
Does not Support: The website or application does not allow the user to display captions if they are available for most videos that have synchronized audio.
Not Applicable: The website or application does not contain video that has synchronized audio.

Supports: When the website or application transmits, converts, or records video with synchronized audio, data associated with captions is preserved, so people who are deaf and others who need captions will be able to access those captions.
Partially Supports: In most cases, when the website or application transmits, converts, or records video with synchronized audio, data associated with captions is preserved
Does not Support: In most, if not all, cases, when the website or application transmits, converts, or records video with synchronized audio, data associated with captions is not preserved
Not Applicable: The website or application does not transmit, convert, or record video that has synchronized audio.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Checkpoint: 11.8.3 Preservation of accessibility information in transformations
Supports: In its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application preserves accessibility information when converting content from one format to another, so some or all of the information in the original format necessary to make portions of the content accessible is provided in the new format, and this content will be available to people with disabilities.
Partially Supports: In most instances, in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application preserves accessibility information when converting content from one format to another, so information in the original format necessary to make portions of the content accessible is provided in the new format, and this content will be available to people with disabilities.
Does not Support: In most, if not all, instances in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application does not preserve accessibility information when converting content from one format to another.
Not Applicable: The website or application is not an authoring tool.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: In its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application provides at least one template that allows the creation of accessible content, so content created using the template(s) will include content that will be accessible to people with disabilities.
Partially Supports: In most instances, in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application provides at least one template that allows the creation of accessible content, so content created using the template(s) will include content that will be accessible to people with disabilities.
Does not Support: In most instances, in its capacity as an authoring tool, the website or application does not provide templates that allow the creation of accessible content, so content created using these templates will include content that will not be accessible to people with disabilities.
Not Applicable: The website or application is not an authoring tool.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 12 - Documentation and Support Svcs.
Checkpoint: 12.2.2 Information on accessibility and compatibility features
Supports: Support services provide information on the website's or application's accessibility features or on features that make it compatible with assistive technology, so people with disabilities will know these features exist and how to use them.
Partially Supports: Support services provide most information on the website's or application's accessibility features or on features that make it compatible with assistive technology, so people with disabilities will know these features exist and how to use them.
Does not Support: Support services do not provide most, if not all, information on the website's or application's accessibility features or on features that make it compatible with assistive technology, so people with disabilities may not know these features exist or how to use them.
Not Applicable: Support services are not provided for the website or application.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Checkpoint: 11.5.2.14 Modification of focus and selection attributes
Supports: For user interface elements that can receive focus, where the focus can be modified by a user and that enable text editing without the use of assistive technology, the focus can be programmatically modified by assistive technologies.
Partially Supports: For most user interface elements that can receive focus, where the focus can be modified by a user and that enable text editing without the use of assistive technology, the focus can be programmatically modified by assistive technologies.
Does not Support: For most, if not all, user interface elements that can receive focus, where the focus can be modified by a user and that enable text editing without the use of assistive technology, the focus cannot be programmatically modified by assistive technologies.
Not Applicable: The ICT does not have a user interface or does not have user interface elements that enable text editing.

Version: EN 301 549 - Chapter 11 - Software (Only 11.7 and 11.8 apply to Web)
Supports: The website or application does not disrupt platform features that are defined in the platform documentation as accessibility features.
Partially Supports: The website or application does not disrupt most platform features that are defined in the platform documentation as accessibility features.
Does not Support: The website or application disrupts most, if not all, platform features that are defined in the platform documentation as accessibility features.
Not Applicable: There are no platform features that are defined in the platform documentation as accessibility features intended for users.
